title: Choose the visual world for ReserBUILD
question: The roll assigned the Turo-turo Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every card is held to neutral colors, as you asked.

options.label: Turo-turo Board
options.lineage: the carinderia's whiteboard of today's dishes and prices
options.thesis: Spaces are listed like the day's dishes: what is free, what it costs, and a marker line through what is taken.
options.viewport: Top bar with the date and time you asked for; below, spaces A–D as board rows with a big right-aligned price; a taken space carries one marker strike and 'Taken'; the cheapest free row leads to Book.
options.risk: If marker lettering leaks from prices into labels, it reads as a food app.

raised.raise: Each space keeps fixed name-plate furniture (letter, type, capacity) that looks the same on every screen.
Hours and amounts are right-aligned in tabular figures, and the charge tally sums exactly to the total, like timed sides that must not overflow.
Each charge segment is drawn at a length exactly proportional to its minutes, so the peak part is visibly the peak part.
The space letter is the one recurring form, used at three fixed sizes only.

options.label: Enlistment Grid
options.lineage: the printed class schedule every student keeps from enlistment
options.thesis: A booking is a block on your week, set like an enlisted class.
options.viewport: A day strip of half-hour rows with A–D as columns; taken blocks shaded like enrolled classes; your chosen 16:00–18:00 drawn as a block with its price.
options.risk: The most familiar card here: close to every calendar app.

options.label: Departures Board
options.thesis: Spaces are departures: each row shows its next free time and its status at a glance.
options.viewport: A black board with A–D as rows, columns for next free time, capacity, and price; a cancelled hold flips back to free.
options.case: Holds product clarity (time and status in rows); loses audience identification, since Manila trains have no flap boards.
options.risk: A dark board on phones in daylight hurts the walk-between-classes use.

options.label: Concourse Sign
options.thesis: Booking is a chain of decisions, and each screen shows only the next one.
options.viewport: A sticky graphite band with the decision in hand ('Pick a space · 16:00–18:00'); the space letters as monumental gate numbers; the signature yellow is translated to graphite for the neutral brief.
options.case: Holds product clarity (one decision at a time on a phone); loses audience identification and its yellow under the neutral pin.
options.risk: Without its yellow the system loses much of its pull.

options.label: Character Catalog
options.thesis: Spaces as a cast of characters.
options.case: Loses both axes: a booking tool is not a cast, and pastels break the neutral pin.
options.kept: Fixed personal furniture per space, identical everywhere.
options.risk: Cute at the cost of trust around money.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.thesis: A booking as a timed side.
options.viewport: Side A / side B as off-peak and peak.
options.case: Loses both axes: nostalgic for this audience and handwritten money reads untrustworthy.
options.kept: Running times right-aligned and the sides never overflow: an exact tally.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.viewport: A pixel-set space letter over dense columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to campus booking, and coarse type hurts WCAG reading.
options.kept: One form repeated at a few fixed sizes.

options.label: Dance Score
options.viewport: Upward time staff with blocks per space.
options.case: Loses both axes: upward time is unfamiliar and the audience does not read scores.
options.risk: Users must learn to read it.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean room-booking app: date and time pickers, a list of room cards, one accent for actions.
canonCard.viewport: Date and time pickers on top, four room cards below with a Book button each.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any booking tool by design.
